title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Grothendieck is in the 'loop equation' part of the Longue Marche continuation. He identifies the profinite completion of pi_{0,3} (free of rank 2, pi_1 of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}) with the completion of Gamma(2)/{±1}. He identifies its S_3-extension, the tilde-pi_{0,3}, with a completion of PSL(2,Z), roughly SL(2,Z)'^. He then maps everything to SL(2,Zhat)/{±1}. In that group act:
- rho, the order-3 symmetry that cyclically permutes 0, 1, infinity;
- sigma_infinity, the symmetry that swaps 0 and 1.
The aim is to test whether the 'loop' relations he has been writing in the profinite fundamental groupoid hold exactly in SL(2,Zhat) after lifting, i.e. with the correct signs. These relations are a precursor of the hexagon relation of Drinfeld's GT, with the factor l_0^nu playing the role of the x^m terms.

This page, step by step.
1. The cusp element is epsilon_0 = ±(1 -1; 0 1), a square root of the loop around 0. Lifting it from SL(2,Zhat)' = SL(2,Zhat)/±1 to SL(2,Zhat) has a sign ambiguity.
2. Margin note: one would like a natural choice of sign. The natural one is the + sign, since that element generates a canonical one-parameter subgroup nu -> (1 -nu; 0 1), nu in Zhat.
3. (39) For l_0 = epsilon_0^2 = (1 -2; 0 1), the generator of inertia at 0 in Gamma(2), there is no sign ambiguity.
4. He asks whether (40) xi = l_0^nu phi (case h=1) and (41) eta = l_0^{-nu} psi (case g=1) hold in SL(2,Zhat) for a suitable sign.
5. Case h=1 is rephrased as data: alpha_0 in tilde-pi^, f in pi_{0,3}^, nu in Zhat, satisfying (42): alpha_0 rho(alpha_0) = l_0^nu f sigma_infinity(f)^{-1}. Here xi = alpha_0 rho(alpha_0) automatically satisfies xi rho(xi) rho^2(xi) = 1.
6. (43) defines:
- xi = alpha_0 rho(alpha_0);
- phi = f sigma_infinity(f)^{-1};
- g = sigma_infinity(f)^{-1} l_1^nu rho(f) = (l_0^nu f)^{-1} (l_0^nu phi) rho(l_0^nu f), using rho(l_0) = l_1.
Thus g is a rho-twisted conjugate of l_0^nu phi.
7. He then lifts alpha_0 and f to (G)L(2,Zhat)^{±1}.

Outcome (next page). One gets xi = epsilon l_0^nu phi with a well-defined sign epsilon. The norm g rho(g) rho^2(g) is invariant under twisted conjugation, and in SL(2,Zhat) one has rho^3 = -1. From these he deduces that epsilon equals the sign epsilon_0 attached to g's norm.

Purpose. This is a sign-bookkeeping verification for the image of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type 'equation des lacets' in the congruence/modular quotient SL(2,Zhat).
errors: No substantive error on this page. The identity sigma_infinity(f)^{-1} l_1^nu rho(f) = (l_0^nu f)^{-1}(l_0^nu phi) rho(l_0^nu f) checks out given phi = f sigma_infinity(f)^{-1} and rho(l_0) = l_1. Note that rho(l_0) = l_1 holds in SL(2,Zhat) without sign only for a suitable lift of rho; the next page asserts this.
Notation drift: the next page writes f sigma_0 f^{-1} where sigma_infinity(f)^{-1} is meant.

ideas.what: Lifting relations from PSL(2,Zhat)-type quotients to SL(2,Zhat): the cusp generator epsilon_0 has a sign ambiguity, its square l_0 does not
ideas.modern_name: central extension SL2 -> PSL2; square root of the parabolic generator at a cusp of Gamma(2)

ideas.what: Loop equation alpha_0 rho(alpha_0) = l_0^nu f sigma_infinity(f)^{-1}, with xi rho(xi) rho^2(xi) = 1 and g a rho-twisted conjugate of l_0^nu phi
ideas.modern_name: precursor of the GT relations: 2-cycle f(x,y)f(y,x)=1 and hexagon f(z,x)z^m f(y,z) y^m f(x,y) x^m = 1
ideas.where_published: Ideas sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); the detailed equations are in unpublished Longue Marche material (unsure)

ideas.what: Twisted conjugation g' = a g rho(a)^{-1} preserves the norm g rho(g) rho^2(g); used together with rho^3 = -1 in SL(2,Zhat) to pin down the sign
ideas.modern_name: twisted conjugacy / nonabelian norm map for an order-3 automorphism

missed.claim: Explicit check of the sign compatibility of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type loop equation in SL(2,Zhat) (rather than PSL), resolved via rho^3 = -1. This is a small bookkeeping detail of Grothendieck's pre-Drinfeld GT computations.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Marginal. It documents that Grothendieck tracked the SL vs PSL lift of the hexagon-type relation, which is relevant to the action of GT on modular/congruence quotients. It is not a new result.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful sign verification within Grothendieck's known (if unpublished) GT-type loop-equation computations. It is historically interesting but routine, with no new theorem.
transcription_corrections: First line: 'de epsilon_0 de Sl(2,Zhat)' dans Sl(2,Zhat)' — the image shows Sl(2,Zhat)' (the quotient by ±1), not a tilde-SL.
Margin note reads roughly 'de même que le signe — on saurait qu'un choix [naturel] ... moins un élément canonique ... engendrant un ss-groupe à 1 paramètre'.
Last line: 'on remonte alpha_0, f dans Gl(2,Zhat)^{±1}' (looks like Gl, not tilde-SL).
Next page (44): 'f sigma_0 f^{-1}' should read 'f sigma_infinity(f)^{-1}'.
